extracted.intended_audience: Users of GAP (computational group theorists, mathematicians and programmers working with finitely presented groups)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference guidelines and behavioural specifications for GAP operations on finitely presented groups: coset tables, augmented coset tables, low-index subgroup searches, quotient algorithms, isomorphism/presentation routines, and Tietze transformations. Covers function semantics, options, defaults, tradeoffs and performance caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetTableStandard
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies the definition of a standard coset table. Its value may be "lenlex" or "semilenlex" and is used whenever coset tables or augmented coset tables are created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If set to "lenlex" coset tables will be standardized using all their columns as defined in Charles Sims’ book (this is the new default standard of GAP). If set to "semilenlex" they will be standardized using only their generator columns (the original GAP standard). The default is "lenlex".

rubrics_metrics.name: StandardizeTable behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: StandardizeTable(table, standard) standardizes the given coset table table. The optional second argument defines the standard to be used ("lenlex" or "semilenlex").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no standard is provided the function uses the global variable CosetTableStandard. Note that the function alters the given table in place; it does not create a copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetTableInWholeGroup semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetTableInWholeGroup(H) (and TryCosetTableInWholeGroup) is equivalent to CosetTable(G,H) where G is the unique finitely presented group such that H is a subgroup of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It overrides a silent option (see CosetTableFromGensAndRels) with false. TryCosetTableInWholeGroup does not override the silent option if coset table computation is expensive; it will store a result that is not fail in the attribute CosetTableInWholeGroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: SubgroupOfWholeGroupByCosetTable requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: SubgroupOfWholeGroupByCosetTable(fpfam, tab) takes a family fpfam of an FpGroup and a standardized coset table tab and returns the subgroup of fpfam!.wholeGroup defined by this coset table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The function will not check whether the coset table is standardized (caller must ensure tab is standardized). See CosetTableBySubgroup for related usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: AugmentedCosetTableInWholeGroup generator guarantee
rubrics_metrics.description: AugmentedCosetTableInWholeGroup(H[, gens]) returns an augmented coset table for subgroup H; if a generator set gens is given, it is guaranteed that gens will be a subset of the primary and secondary subgroup generators of this coset table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The augmented coset table is mutable so further entries may be added, but existing entries must not be changed. Added entries should correspond to the subgroup only and not to a homomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: AugmentedCosetTable mutability constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Augmented coset tables are mutable, permitting addition of further entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing entries may not be changed. Any entries added should correspond to the subgroup only and not to a homomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: AugmentedCosetTableMtc purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: AugmentedCosetTableMtc(G, H, type, string) applies a Modified Todd-Coxeter coset representative enumeration to construct an augmented coset table for subgroup H of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is an internal function used by subgroup presentation functions; subgroup generators will be named string1, string2, .... It accepts options (e.g., max and silent) as described for CosetTableFromGensAndRels.

rubrics_metrics.name: AugmentedCosetTableRrs purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: AugmentedCosetTableRrs(G, table, type, string) applies the Reduced Reidemeister–Schreier method to construct an augmented coset table for the subgroup of G defined by the given coset table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new subgroup generators will be named string1, string2, .... It is used internally by subgroup presentation functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: RewriteWord semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: RewriteWord(aug, word) rewrites a word (a word in the underlying free group) in the subgroup generators given by the augmented coset table aug.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It returns a Tietze-type word (list of integers) referring to the primary and secondary generators of aug. If word is not contained in the subgroup, it returns fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: LowIndexSubgroupsFpGroup usage and return
rubrics_metrics.description: LowIndexSubgroupsFpGroupIterator(G[, H], index[, excluded]) and LowIndexSubgroupsFpGroup(G[, H], index[, excluded]) compute representatives of conjugacy classes of subgroups of finitely presented group G that contain subgroup H and have index ≤ index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LowIndexSubgroupsFpGroupIterator returns an iterator; LowIndexSubgroupsFpGroup returns the list. If interested only in one or a few subgroups up to a given index prefer the iterator. If excluded is provided (list of words) the returned subgroups must not contain conjugates of elements defined by those words. If H is omitted it defaults to the trivial subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: LowIndexSubgroupsFpGroup performance caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: The algorithm finds subgroups by systematically running through a tree of all potential coset tables of length at most index, skipping branches that cannot provide new classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time required depends on the presentation of G but in general grows exponentially with index. Be careful with the choice of index.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismFpGroup purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: IsomorphismFpGroup(G) returns an isomorphism from a given finite group G to a finitely presented group isomorphic to G by choosing generators and computing a presentation in those generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to convert concrete finite groups into finitely presented form; see examples for returned presentations/relators.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismFpGroupByGenerators objective and NC variant
rubrics_metrics.description: IsomorphismFpGroupByGenerators(G, gens[, string]) returns an isomorphism from a finite group G to a finitely presented group F whose generators correspond to gens. IsomorphismFpGroupByGeneratorsNC avoids testing whether gens generate G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If string is given it names the generators of F. The main task is to find a presentation in the provided generators, using stabilizer chains and multi-stage relations-finding; Tietze transformations are used to avoid explosion of relator length.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismFpGroupByGenerators randomness and differing outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Because random methods are involved (in construction of stabilizer chains), repeated calls with the same arguments may produce different resulting presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware results may vary across runs; use options/method to influence strategy when reproducibility or specific sizes are desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismFpGroupByGenerators method options and tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Option method may be "regular", ["regular", bound], "fast", or "default" to modify the strategy used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "regular": construct a regular representation R and then a presentation of R (concise presentation but expensive). ["regular", bound]: apply "regular" to the largest stabilizer whose size ≤ bound, then multi-stage algorithm. "fast": multi-stage without attempts to reduce number/length of relators (faster but may produce huge relator length). "default": default method. The method affects performance and results; for matrix groups the option can be relevant because NiceMonomorphism may produce a permutation group to which the method applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsomorphismSimplifiedFpGroup objective
rubrics_metrics.description: IsomorphismSimplifiedFpGroup(G) applies Tietze transformations to a copy of the presentation of G to reduce number of generators, number of relators, and relator lengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It returns an isomorphism with range a group H isomorphic to G whose presentation has been simplified via Tietze transformations. See section on Tietze transforms for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage of long subgroup element words
rubrics_metrics.description: When working with homomorphisms to finitely presented images, subgroup elements may be expressed as extremely long words; underlying words and preimages are stored as straight line program elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These straight line program elements behave like ordinary words; EvalStraightLineProgElm can be used to convert them back to ordinary word form if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient algorithms and available quotient types
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP provides quotient algorithms for finitely presented groups to compute epimorphisms onto abelian groups, p-groups, solvable groups, and via low-index methods permutation group quotients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include MaximalAbelianQuotient, PQuotient, EpimorphismPGroup, EpimorphismNilpotentQuotient, SolvableQuotient, and GQuotients which computes all epimorphisms onto a given finite group.

rubrics_metrics.name: PQuotient parameters and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: PQuotient(F,p[,c][,logord][,ctype]) computes a factor p-group quotient system; parameter c sets p-class, logord limits order via p^logord, ctype selects collector type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If c omitted algorithm attempts to compute largest factor p-group and may not terminate. Default computes only with factor groups of order at most p^256. If logord is present, c must be given; implementation errors if order exceeds p^256 or p^logord. ctype must be "single" or "combinatorial" controlling collector implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: EpimorphismQuotientSystem semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: EpimorphismQuotientSystem(quotsys) returns an epimorphism F → P where quotsys is a quotient system from PQuotient, F the source finitely presented group and P a pc group isomorphic to the quotient determined by quotsys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different calls create different groups P, each with its own family; typical usage example shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: EpimorphismPGroup and EpimorphismNilpotentQuotient usage
rubrics_metrics.description: EpimorphismPGroup(fpgrp,p[,cl]) computes an epimorphism to the largest p-group quotient of specified p-class; EpimorphismNilpotentQuotient(fpgrp[,n]) returns epimorphism on class-n finite nilpotent quotient (or largest within bounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cl/n omitted the largest finite quotient up to implementation class bounds is returned (p-class up to 1000 in current description). Examples demonstrate sizes obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: SolvableQuotient input modes
rubrics_metrics.description: SolvableQuotient(F, size) / SolvableQuotient(F, primes) / SolvableQuotient(F, tuples) compute solvable quotients specified by maximum size, primes involved, or prescribed chief series tuples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SQ can be used as synonym. EpimorphismSolvableQuotient(F,param) computes epimorphism to largest solvable quotient given by param.

rubrics_metrics.name: LargerQuotientBySubgroupAbelianization intent
rubrics_metrics.description: LargerQuotientBySubgroupAbelianization(hom, U) attempts to return subgroup S ≤ G such that core(S) is properly contained in ker(hom) and in the derived subgroup of V (preimage of U), exposing a larger quotient of G; returns fail if none exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to search for larger quotients via subgroup abelianizations; example shows substantial growth in quotient size.

rubrics_metrics.name: AbelianInvariantsSubgroupFpGroup methods
rubrics_metrics.description: AbelianInvariantsSubgroupFpGroup(G,H) (and suffix variants Mtc / Rrs) compute abelian invariants of a subgroup H using either Modified Todd-Coxeter (Mtc) or Reduced Reidemeister–Schreier (Rrs) methods; alternatively a coset table can be supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AbelianInvariantsSubgroupFpGroup is a synonym for the Rrs variant. Use these when you want control over method used to compute abelian invariants without full subgroup presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing finiteness caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no general algorithm to test finiteness of a finitely presented group; GAP's IsFinite tries to find (via coset enumeration) a cyclic subgroup of finite index and rewrites the presentation to that subgroup if found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because no bound on index is known, the test might continue unsuccessfully until memory is exhausted. Several methods exist to prove a group infinite, none guaranteed to work in every case: using LowIndexSubgroups to find U with infinite [U:U'] (checked via IsInfiniteAbelianizationGroup), or NewmanInfinityCriterion based on p-group quotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsInfiniteAbelianizationGroup purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: IsInfiniteAbelianizationGroup(G) returns true if commutator factor group G/G' is infinite; may do so without computing full structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful as a faster check when trying to prove groups infinite instead of computing full AbelianInvariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: NewmanInfinityCriterion applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: NewmanInfinityCriterion(G,p) applies an infinity criterion due to M. F. Newman for prime p dividing order of commutator factor group; returns true if criterion proves G infinite and fail otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criterion depends on the number of generators and relations in the presentation; reducing the presentation via Tietze transformations (IsomorphismSimplifiedFpGroup) may make criterion more effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: PresentationFpGroup behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: PresentationFpGroup(G[, printlevel]) creates a Tietze presentation object for finitely presented group G; this presentation is exactly as G's presentation with no initial Tietze transformations applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional printlevel controls messages from later Tietze transformations applied to the created presentation (0 suppresses, 1 default interactive, 2 extra output).

rubrics_metrics.name: TzSort and relator ordering note
rubrics_metrics.description: Most functions creating presentations and all functions performing Tietze transformations sort relators by increasing length; TzSort(P) explicitly sorts relators of presentation P by increasing lengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PresentationFpGroup is an exception (it preserves the original relator ordering). TzSort modifies P in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: GeneratorsOfPresentation semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: GeneratorsOfPresentation(P) returns a list of free generators that is a shallow copy of the current generators of presentation P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to inspect or reuse generator list; returned list is a shallow copy (see ShallowCopy documentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: FpGroupPresentation and PresentationViaCosetTable differences
rubrics_metrics.description: FpGroupPresentation(P[, nam]) constructs an f.p. group from a Tietze presentation P. PresentationViaCosetTable(G[, F, words]) constructs a presentation for a concrete finite group G using relations-finding algorithms and automatically applies Tietze transformations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PresentationViaCosetTable: if only G specified single-stage algorithm used; providing F and words triggers two-stage algorithm which constructs coset tables of sizes |H| and |G|/|H| saving space. Before returning, presentation is simplified but without allowing elimination of generators to preserve bijection between generators of G and presentation; call SimplifyPresentation afterward if eliminations are acceptable. PresentationViaCosetTable usually better than PresentationFpGroup for obtaining new presentations; IsomorphismFpGroup is recommended to convert to an f.p. group object.

rubrics_metrics.name: PresentationViaCosetTable simplification policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PresentationViaCosetTable simplifies the resulting presentation by calling SimplifyPresentation but disallows eliminations of generators to retain bijection between list of generators of G and presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If generators of G are redundant and bijection not needed, call SimplifyPresentation again without that restriction to obtain a shorter presentation.
